profile.reading:
This OSM record, named simply "Switch12" and distinct from the separately tracked "Switch Las Vegas 12" record in this dataset, is tagged near Switch's Las Vegas Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, but could not be confirmed as an actual Switch data center this session. A reverse geocode of this record's own stored coordinates returned the address of GES, Global Experience Specialists, an unrelated events and exhibition-services company at 7000 Lindell Road, Las Vegas, not a Switch facility, and no data center industry aggregator directory lists a facility distinctly named "Switch 12" or "Switch12" separate from the already-confirmed Las Vegas 12 building at its own distinct Capovilla Avenue address. Switch's own official locations page publishes no individual building addresses at all, directing visitors instead to a contact form, so this record cannot be cross-checked against a direct operator statement either. This record most plausibly represents either a duplicate or stale mapping of the confirmed Las Vegas 12 building, a genuine but unidentified additional Switch structure whose coordinates were recorded inaccurately, or a mapping error unrelated to Switch entirely; this profile does not assert any of these possibilities as fact given the lack of corroborating evidence, consistent with this dataset's practice of documenting genuine ambiguity rather than guessing at a resolution. Switch's Core Campus overall, of which this record is presumed to be some part given its Clark County, Nevada location and Switch-branded name, is marketed as offering up to 495 megawatts of power upon completion and 100 percent renewable energy.

Switch's broader Las Vegas Core Campus, of which the confirmed Las Vegas 12 building sits nearby, has grown from Rob Roy's original 2002 acquisition of a former Enron-affiliated facility into eleven or more operating buildings spanning well over 2 million square feet, with Switch's current marketing describing up to 495 megawatts of power available upon full campus completion. Clark County's data center cluster, anchored substantially by Switch, has drawn additional colocation and hyperscale investment from other operators over the past decade, reinforcing Las Vegas as a significant secondary U.S. data center market outside the major coastal and Northern Virginia hubs.

This record's identity is unresolved. A reverse geocode of the stored coordinates points to an events company, not a data center, and no independent aggregator lists a distinct "Switch 12" facility separate from the already-confirmed Switch Las Vegas 12 building at a different address. The record is likely a duplicate mapping, stale coordinates, or an error unrelated to Switch entirely. Switch's own locations page publishes no individual building addresses, so the claim cannot be verified against an operator statement.

The broader Switch Las Vegas Core Campus, of which this record is presumed some part, operates eleven or more buildings across over 2 million square feet and markets up to 495 megawatts of total power upon full completion. If this campus's published capacity were achieved, it would rank third among Nevada facilities with a published megawatt figure, though only two facilities in the state publish capacity at all. The campus is marketed as powered entirely by renewable energy.

Because the facility's identity and location remain unconfirmed, no reliable statement can be made about its current operational status, available capacity, or relevance to AI infrastructure scaling. Any assessment of this record must await either corrected coordinates, a direct operator statement, or confirmation via Clark County property records.
